title: They Kissed, But God Wasn’t There
paragraphs: They Kissed, But God Wasn’t There
Why the deepest craving in your soul will never be satisfied by skin alone
There are people lying next to someone they can touch… but still feeling completely untouched.

Hands intertwined. Bodies close. Breathing the same air. Yet something inside them is starving, aching, hollow in a way they can’t explain. They thought physical closeness would quiet the loneliness, but instead it exposed something deeper… something louder.
Because the soul was never designed to be fulfilled by flesh.

There is a reason why even after intimacy, some people stare at the ceiling in silence, wondering why they still feel empty. It’s because what they’re truly craving is not physical connection… it’s spiritual union.
And most people don’t even realize the difference.

In the beginning, before sin fractured everything, intimacy wasn’t first physical—it was spiritual. Genesis 2:25 says in Hebrew, “וַיִּהְיוּ שְׁנֵיהֶם עֲרוּמִּים… וְלֹא יִתְבֹּשָׁשׁוּ” (vayihyu shneihem arummim… velo yitboshashu) — “They were both naked… and were not ashamed.”
This wasn’t just about bodies without clothes. It was about souls without walls.
No hiding. No pretending. No performing.
That’s the kind of intimacy we were created for.

But sin entered, and suddenly they covered themselves. Not just physically—but spiritually. Shame was born. Distance was born. And ever since then, humanity has been trying to recreate intimacy through physical means, while ignoring the spiritual fracture underneath.

That’s why physical intimacy without spiritual intimacy often leads to confusion, attachment, heartbreak, and emptiness. It feels real in the moment… but fades quickly because it was never designed to carry the weight of your soul.

The Greek word for “flesh” in the New Testament is “σάρξ” (sarx). It represents not just the body, but the fallen human nature—temporary, unstable, driven by impulse. But the word for spirit is “πνεῦμα” (pneuma)—the breath of God, the eternal part of you that longs for Him.
You can satisfy the sarx for a moment.
But only God can satisfy the pneuma.
And this is where everything changes.
Because true intimacy is not when someone sees your body.
It’s when God reaches your spirit.
Psalm 42:7 says, “Deep calls to deep.” In Hebrew, “תְּהוֹם אֶל־תְּהוֹם קוֹרֵא” (tehom el-tehom qore). This is not surface-level connection. This is soul calling out to soul.
And nothing shallow can answer a deep call.
That’s why you can be desired physically… but still feel unseen spiritually.
That’s why you can be wanted… but not known.
And that’s why some of the most “intimate” relationships are actually the loneliest.
Because without God at the center, intimacy becomes consumption instead of covenant.
But Jesus didn’t come to give you a temporary feeling.
He came to restore your capacity for real intimacy.

In John 15:15, Jesus says, “I no longer call you servants… I have called you friends.” The Greek word for friend here is “φίλους” (philous)—a deep relational closeness, not transactional, not distant.
Jesus is inviting you into spiritual intimacy with Him.
Not religion.
Not performance.
Not pretending.
But closeness.
Honest, raw, soul-level connection.

And once you experience that kind of intimacy with Christ, everything else changes. You stop chasing people to fill what only God can fulfill. You stop confusing physical closeness for emotional security. You stop settling for surface-level connection.
Because your spirit has finally been touched.
And here’s the truth many don’t want to admit…
Some people are addicted to physical intimacy because they are starving for spiritual intimacy.
They are trying to heal a soul wound with a body experience.
But it will never be enough.
It can’t be.
Because your soul belongs to God.
And until it returns to Him, it will always feel restless.
Augustine said it best, “Our hearts are restless until they rest in You.”
And maybe that’s you right now.
Maybe you’ve been searching.
Maybe you’ve been giving parts of yourself away, hoping someone would finally see you, choose you, stay.
But deep down… you’re tired.
Tired of temporary connections.
Tired of emotional confusion.
Tired of feeling empty after moments that were supposed to mean something.
Be honest.
This hit harder than you expected, didn’t it?
Because healing begins with honesty.
Jesus is not asking for your perfection.
He’s asking for your openness.
Revelation 3:20 says, “Behold, I stand at the door and knock…” In Greek, “ἰδοὺ ἕστηκα ἐπὶ τὴν θύραν καὶ κρούω” (idou hestēka epi tēn thuran kai krouō).
He’s not forcing His way in.
He’s waiting for you to open the door.
Not to your body.
But to your heart.
And when you do… everything changes.
Because spiritual intimacy with Christ doesn’t leave you empty.
It fills you, transforms you, restores you, and teaches you what real love actually feels like.
Love that doesn’t use you.
Love that doesn’t leave you.
Love that doesn’t fade.
If this spoke to you, don’t keep it to yourself.
Because surface-level faith will never sustain you in deep battles.
We go deeper here.
Because this isn’t about content.
It’s about transformation.
Stay close.
Because the closer you get to Jesus, the less anything counterfeit will satisfy you.
And that loneliness you’ve been trying to silence…
was never meant to be filled by another person.
It was always meant to lead you back to Him.
The kind of intimacy your soul is craving has a name—and it’s Jesus.
